_about: Names that get no baby-name page (design 3.2). Each entry: the name as the Berean spells it, and why. The build fails if an entry matches nothing, so this list stays true. 'formOnly': the name is not a page but must never be used as another spelling either.

names.name: Christ
names.reason: A title of Jesus (Messiah, 'anointed'), not a given name; it belongs with the Names of God page at /study/names.

names.name: Messiah
names.reason: A title of Jesus that TIPNR lists as another form of his name; it must not become a redirect to the Jesus page.

names.name: Baal
names.reason: The name of a pagan god (also borne by one obscure Benjamite); not offered as a baby name.

names.name: Baal-zebub
names.reason: A Philistine god (Beelzebul, a name for Satan in the Gospels).

names.name: Adrammelech
names.reason: An Assyrian god (2 Kings 17:31); the same name is borne by Sennacherib's murderous son.

names.name: Anammelech
names.reason: An Assyrian god worshipped with child sacrifice (2 Kings 17:31).

names.name: Pharaoh
names.reason: A title of Egypt's kings, not a given name.

names.name: Caesar
names.reason: A title of the Roman emperors, not a given name.

names.name: Hittite
names.reason: A people's name (the clan of Heth), not a given name.

names.name: Greek
names.reason: A people's name, not a given name.

names.name: Jew
names.reason: A people's designation, not a person's given name. Galatians 2:14 uses it for Jewish identity; Strong's G2450 and G2452 describe Judaizing/Jewish practice, not the personal name Judah.

names.name: Zealot
names.reason: Simon's epithet in Luke 6:15, not a given name (Strong's G2208); Simon keeps his own name page.

names.name: Iscariot
names.reason: Judas's epithet (probably 'man of Kerioth'), not a given name; Judas has his own page.

names.name: Tartan
names.reason: An Assyrian office (the army's commander-in-chief), printed 'the Tartan' in the Berean (2 Kings 18:17, Isaiah 20:1); a title, not a given name, like Pharaoh.

names.name: Rabshakeh
names.reason: An Assyrian office (the chief cupbearer or field commander), always printed 'the Rabshakeh' in the Berean; a title, not a given name.
